subject: Subprocessor residency assessment & evidence timeline for NexaHealth
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@nexahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: NexaHealth Procurement <procurement@nexahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: subprocessor residency + SIG/CAIQ scope

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of NexaHealth's vendor intake I need a short residency assessment and the supporting evidence for Redwood's key subprocessors. Specifically we need: 

- A roster of subprocessors with country/region of data processing (onshore/EU/APAC) and whether they hold customer data or encryption keys.
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest) or access instructions.
- KMS/residency ownership details (who holds keys, any HSM/KMS providers, where keys reside).
- SIG/CAIQ completion status and any outstanding artifacts.

Can you provide an initial roster and SOC2 by EOD May 20? Procurement will need SIG/CAIQ and KMS matrix by May 24. If anything needs an NDA or DocuSign step before we share logs, flag it.

Appreciate a quick heads-up on scope (down-to-transitive-subprocessors vs. top-level vendors).

Best,
Emily
Emily Park
Security Program Manager, NexaHealth
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <epark@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor residency + SIG/CAIQ scope

Hi Emily,

Thanks — we're on it. Attached is an initial CSV (redwood_subprocessor_roster_v1.csv) that lists current production subprocessors at the top level (service name, primary country, processes customer data: yes/no, holds keys: yes/no). I've also attached our latest SOC2 Type II (redacted) for immediate review.

Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:
- Do you need transitive subprocessors (i.e., our vendors' vendors) enumerated now, or is a top-level roster sufficient for procurement?
- For KMS: do you want logical ownership (we manage keys via Redwood KMS + AWS KMS for some flows) or physical residency per provider? We can provide both; the KMS matrix will include provider, region, and whether key escrow/rotation is customer-initiated.

Planned next steps (tentative):
- Today: send CSV + SOC2 stub (attached).
- Mon/Tue: follow up with KMS residency matrix and a one-page dataflow narrative you can give to procurement.
- By May 24: SIG/CAIQ status and remaining artifacts.

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min sync next week to walk through any high-risk entries.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor residency + SIG/CAIQ scope

Mina — adding a few internal notes before we send the KMS matrix: 

- For any subprocessors that 'hold keys: yes' we should indicate whether keys are customer-generated (BYOK) or Redwood-managed. That will change the procurement risk posture.
- Add a column for 'transfer encryption in transit' and 'at-rest encryption (provider default/managed)'.
- Include a short comment field on whether we have SOC2 or other attestation from that vendor.

Irene: can you prepare a short attestation paragraph for our KMS approach (BYOK options, HSM usage where applicable) that Mina can drop into the one-page narrative?

Mina: I'll review the CSV and flag any high-risk vendors (PCI, PHI processing) — I think there are 3 items we should pre-annotate.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Vendor Security
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:46:00 -0700

Mina / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of procurement asks to call out: 

- Procurement requires a one-page vendor security summary that they can attach to the PO. That should include: high-level data flow (where PHI touches Redwood), key custody model, and primary geo of processing. 
- We also need the CAIQ completion status for SIG — we don't need the full completed SIG in the initial pass, but we do want the missing/partial items enumerated so we can understand gaps.

Note: our legal team will request an NDA/limited DocuSign if we need access to logs or non-redacted telemetry. Assume we won't be able to exchange any debug logs until that's in place.

Proposed timeline: SOC2 + top-level roster by May 20 (ok per your note). SIG/CAIQ and KMS matrix by May 24. Full transitive list by June 3 if needed. Can you confirm?

Best,
Tom Lane
Director, Procurement — NexaHealth
